interpretation_limits: SFH_SURFACE_NEUTRAL is a required arm name, not a claim of token neutrality, matched token count, or perfect semantic equivalence; its declarative wording and tokenization differ from SFH_RAW_NATIVE.

The raw-versus-surface comparison changes the raw article-bearing first sentence 'I recommend the <archived target>.' to the declarative '<archived target> was my choice.' while holding native roles, history user content, selected target, and assistant second sentence fixed; it still changes wording and tokens and therefore supports only a bounded surface-frame association in these cases.
The current-restatement baseline changes recency, prompt length, and repeated content together; the format reminder changes instruction recency and prompt length together.
Exact frozen-target categories miss paraphrases and cannot establish absence of broader historical influence.
The finite selection grammar prevents known exact-target surface variants from being mislabeled as unknown, but it intentionally leaves paraphrases and unregistered syntax in NONE.
A history_template_copy score detects only the literal normalized prefix 'i recommend the '; it is not evidence of semantic memory copying or a causal mechanism.
Synthetic controlled-choice behavior is not real-speaker dialogue behavior, broad Persona Fidelity, independent validation, cross-model evidence, or an algorithmic contribution.
Each synthetic persona contributes one case; leave-one-persona-out sensitivity cannot separate persona effects from case effects.
